question: How do medications interact with our cells?

options.A: By permanently replacing vital organs with chemical substitutes
options.B: By modifying or blocking already existing cellular activities
options.C: By changing the basic genetic code of the target organ
options.D: By destroying diseased cells and generating brand new tissues

explanation: Great job! Think of drugs as little keys that speed up, slow down, or block processes your body already knows how to do. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h1)

question: A student nurse uses old patient admission files from last year to study malaria rates. What kind of data source is this?

options.A: Subjective data source
options.B: Secondary data source
options.C: Primary data source
options.D: Experimental data source

explanation: Because someone else collected those files in the past, you are using a secondary source. It's like hand-me-down data! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which lab value or vital sign must be checked regularly for patients on long-term corticosteroids?

options.A: Liver enzyme AST
options.B: Blood glucose levels
options.C: Red blood cell count
options.D: Serum creatinine

explanation: Correct! Steroids trigger the liver to release stored sugar, which often leads to high blood sugar levels that need close monitoring. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h7)

question: To prevent lung infections in a patient on a ventilator, what angle should the head of their bed be elevated?

options.A: 90 degrees upright
options.B: 0 to 10 degrees
options.C: 60 to 75 degrees
options.D: 30 to 45 degrees

explanation: Keeping the bed raised between 30 and 45 degrees uses gravity to stop oral secretions and stomach contents from sliding down into the lungs. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h5)

question: A nurse needs to give an IM vaccine to a healthy adult. Which site is the most appropriate choice?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Abdomen
options.C: Dorsogluteal
options.D: Vastus lateralis

explanation: The deltoid muscle is easily accessible and standard for routine adult vaccinations like tetanus or influenza. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why is it important to include the family when creating a patient's care plan?

options.A: It legally forces the family to pay all hospital bills
options.B: It ensures the plan fits their routine and improves cooperation
options.C: It stops the doctor from making any changes to the treatment
options.D: It reduces the total number of nursing shifts required

explanation: When families help build the plan, they understand it better and are much more likely to help carry it out at home. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h6)

question: Near the end of life, what is the primary focus of palliative psychological care?

options.A: Finding a sudden cure for the advanced condition
options.B: Promoting comfort, dignity, and emotional peace
options.C: Preventing family members from visiting the patient
options.D: Encouraging aggressive life-extending surgeries

explanation: Palliative care centers entirely on quality of life, surrounding the patient with warmth, respect, and peace. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h6)

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely performed on a newborn?

options.A: One and five minutes after birth
options.B: Immediately at birth and thirty minutes later
options.C: Ten and twenty minutes after birth
options.D: Every fifteen minutes for the first hour

explanation: The Apgar score is systematically calculated at one minute and five minutes after birth to evaluate the newborn's immediate adjustment to extrauterine life and response to resuscitation if needed. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: Why are pancreatic protein-digesting enzymes released in an inactive form like trypsinogen?

options.A: To allow them to survive the high acid of the stomach
options.B: To prevent the enzymes from digesting the pancreas itself
options.C: To ensure they only work when mixed with saliva
options.D: To slow down digestion until the food reaches the large intestine

explanation: It's a clever safety mechanism! If these powerful enzymes were active inside the pancreas, they would chew up the organ's own tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the main difference between nutritional screening and a full nutritional assessment?

options.A: Screening is done by doctors, while assessment is done by cooks
options.B: Screening is only used for children, while assessment is for adults
options.C: Screening is a quick check to find risk, while assessment is a deep dive
options.D: Screening only looks at lab work, while assessment only looks at weight

explanation: Screening quickly identifies who is at risk, prompting a thorough assessment to diagnose specific nutritional problems. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h4)

question: A nurse uses self-awareness to connect authentically with a frightened patient. Which pattern of knowing is this?

options.A: Personal knowing
options.B: Empirical knowing
options.C: Aesthetic knowing
options.D: Ethical knowing

explanation: Personal knowing is about looking inward and using self-reflection to build a genuine, trusting relationship with your patient. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h2)

question: If a delay in the hospital pharmacy slows down when a ward nurse can teach a patient about their discharge drugs, what does this show?

options.A: Traditional epistemological habit
options.B: Appreciation of a system
options.C: Individual cognitive bias
options.D: Understanding clinical variation

explanation: Spot on! This shows how one part of the hospital (pharmacy) directly links to and affects another part (the ward nurse's workflow). [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why is feeling the uterus during a physical assessment so important when suspecting postpartum endometritis?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the organ
options.B: To check for tenderness and a boggy texture
options.C: To test the strength of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: To evaluate the size of the ovaries

explanation: A healthy postpartum uterus should feel firm as it shrinks back down. An infected one feels tender and soft, or 'boggy,' because it's struggling to contract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h5)

question: Which type of accident causes the highest number of injuries and trauma on Nigerian roads?

options.A: Road traffic accidents
options.B: Commercial flight crashes
options.C: Skiing and snowboarding falls
options.D: Mountain climbing injuries

explanation: Crashes involving cars, commercial buses, motorcycles, and pedestrians are among the leading causes of trauma in our country. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h2)

question: Why does calling FGM a human rights violation make such a big difference in healthcare and law?

options.A: It makes prosecution of offenders completely unnecessary in local courts
options.B: It grants healthcare workers the right to perform the procedure safely
options.C: It redefines the practice from a tradition to a punishable act of violence
options.D: It removes the need for community education and legal penalties

explanation: You got it! Labeling FGM as a human rights abuse takes it out of the 'harmless culture' box, making it clear to everyone that it is harmful and unlawful. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which big international agreement officially made Primary Health Care the standard for health for all?

options.A: The Abuja Malaria Treaty
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Accord
options.C: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.D: The Nightingale Pact

explanation: Spot on! The 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration set the global goal of making basic healthcare accessible to every individual and family. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h4)

question: What happens in the body when Beta-2 adrenergic receptors are stimulated?

options.A: Relaxation of smooth muscle in the airways
options.B: Decrease in overall heart rate and force
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: Increased production of digestive fluids

explanation: Think of Beta-2 receptors as the keys that open up the airways! When stimulated, they relax the smooth muscles in the lungs so air can flow easily. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which measure of central tendency is appropriate for nominal data like patient blood types?

options.A: Mode
options.B: Average
options.C: Mean
options.D: Median

explanation: Blood types are categories, not numbers. Therefore, you can only count which category shows up most often—which is the mode! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why do nurses divide adolescence into different stages?

options.A: It removes the need to talk directly to the patient
options.B: It proves that teenagers will always rebel against authority
options.C: It helps identify normal milestones versus clinical problems
options.D: It stops physical growth from happening too quickly

explanation: Spot on! Breaking adolescence down into stages helps you anticipate what changes are normal and catch any health or developmental delays early. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of a respiratory assessment?

options.A: To check the client for peripheral edema
options.B: To evaluate oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange
options.C: To determine the primary cause of a heart attack
options.D: To measure the exact lung capacity in liters

explanation: Respiratory assessment focuses directly on how well the lungs are moving air and exchanging gases to keep tissues oxygenated. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h1)

question: How do protective bed accessories help keep a patient's skin safe and healthy?

options.A: By acting as buffers between the body and the mattress
options.B: By increasing natural skin moisture and sweat production
options.C: By stimulating local sweat gland activity
options.D: By sealing skin pores to block bacteria entry

explanation: Spot on! These accessories create soft barriers that reduce direct friction and crushing pressure on vulnerable skin areas. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do right after using a surgical instrument at the bedside?

options.A: Wipe away gross debris to prevent drying
options.B: Spray the metal with industrial lubricating oil
options.C: Place the item directly into an autoclave chamber
options.D: Submerge the instrument in concentrated bleach

explanation: Always do a quick pre-wipe! If blood and tissue dry onto the metal, they become ten times harder to clean later. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why might a country with a growing economy still have poor public health funding?

options.A: Private citizens refuse to use public healthcare facilities
options.B: Hospitals are legally barred from receiving federal tax revenue
options.C: Economic growth automatically decreases the total population size
options.D: Government policy priorities may direct funds away from the health sector

explanation: Even if money is being made, leaders can choose to spend it on other things like defense or roads instead of healthcare. Politics matters for nurses too! [learn more](GST322_U3_T6#GST322_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the main function of social health insurance schemes?

options.A: Pooling resources so healthy people help pay for the sick
options.B: Paying salaries exclusively for hospital administrators
options.C: Making private insurance companies bankrupt
options.D: Eliminating all government taxes on food

explanation: Health insurance spreads financial risk by collecting small regular payments from many people to cover the few who fall ill. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which imaging test uses contrast dye and X-rays to clearly view the inside of the uterus and fallopian tubes?

options.A: Transvaginal ultrasound
options.B: Saline infusion sonohysterography
options.C: Hysterosalpingography
options.D: Abdominal CT scan

explanation: Correct! Hysterosalpingography (HSG) combines 'hystero' (uterus), 'salpingo' (tubes), and 'graphy' (imaging) using dye to see if the tubes are open. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of 'organizing' in nursing management?

options.A: Measuring patient health outcomes after discharge
options.B: Arranging resources, roles, and workflows to achieve goals
options.C: Writing the hospital mission statement
options.D: Motivating employees through public praise

explanation: Organizing is about setting up your environment and tools so that your plans can actually happen without stress. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the name of the thick muscular middle layer of the heart wall that pumps blood?

options.A: Myocardium
options.B: Epicardium
options.C: Pericardium
options.D: Endocardium

explanation: The myocardium is the muscular middle layer of the heart that does the hard work of contracting and pumping blood to the body! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main goal of different health sectors working together?

options.A: To increase the cost of specialized medical equipment
options.B: To coordinate care and improve community health outcomes
options.C: To eliminate all private hospitals from the healthcare system
options.D: To reduce the total number of practicing nurses in a region

explanation: Teamwork across different health areas helps us share resources and close gaps in patient care. You'll see this often in community postings! [learn more](GST322_U5_T3#GST322_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why are anti-nausea meds usually given before chemo starts instead of waiting for nausea to begin?

options.A: Preventing nausea before it starts is much more effective than treating it later
options.B: They help the patient fall asleep during the long infusion
options.C: Chemotherapy drugs will not dissolve properly without them
options.D: They taste better when taken on an empty stomach

explanation: Prevention is key! Giving these meds early blocks the vomiting center before chemo triggers it. Brilliant clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which quick physical check is critical before prescribing a combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive?

options.A: Chest X-ray imaging
options.B: Fasting blood glucose test
options.C: Blood pressure measurement
options.D: Routine eye examination

explanation: Always check the BP first! Estrogen can sometimes cause blood pressure to rise or increase clot risks, so checking baseline BP keeps your client safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h5)

question: You are preparing a suction catheter for an adult patient with an artificial airway. What is the rule of thumb for selecting the catheter size?

options.A: It must be the largest possible size that fits through the opening
options.B: It should always be a uniform size 14 French regardless of the tube
options.C: It should fill the entire inside of the tube to grab all the mucus
options.D: It should take up no more than half the inner diameter of the airway

explanation: Leaving enough open space around the catheter prevents a vacuum from forming inside the lungs, which would dangerously drop oxygen levels. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: When is the best time to start palliative care for someone with a serious illness?

options.A: After the patient is discharged to a nursing home
options.B: Exclusively during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.C: Early in the disease process alongside curative treatments
options.D: Only when all curative treatments have failed

explanation: Great thinking! Palliative care isn't just for the very end. It works best when started right alongside regular medical treatments from the time of diagnosis to support the patient all through their journey. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant patient on insulin therapy tells the nurse she feels shaky, sweaty, and dizzy. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Wait thirty minutes to see if symptoms resolve
options.B: Administer a rapid-acting insulin injection
options.C: Provide a fast-acting oral carbohydrate source
options.D: Collect a routine venous blood sample for HbA1c

question: What happens when you mix two bases that don't go together?

options.C: The chemical formula permanently turns into a solid block
options.D: The active medication becomes twice as strong

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the difference between the incubation period and the latent period?

options.A: Symptoms always start at the exact same hour infectiousness begins
options.B: Latent periods only apply to non-infectious chronic illnesses
options.C: Incubation periods tell nurses when to discharge patients
options.D: A person may be able to spread the disease before showing any symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes the latent period is shorter than the incubation period, meaning someone can spread an infection while still feeling completely well. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is the proper way to remove a honeybee stinger stuck in the skin?

options.A: Scrape it gently across the skin using a flat, rigid edge
options.B: Burn the stinger with a heated match to neutralize the venom
options.C: Squeeze the venom sac tightly with metal tweezers and pull straight out
options.D: Scrub the area vigorously with a stiff surgical brush

question: Why do we usually need to treat everyone in a household if just one person has pinworms?

options.C: Pinworms spread easily among people living in close contact

question: How do heavy house chores negatively affect a school girl's education?

options.A: They leave her exhausted with little time left to study or attend classes

options.C: They improve her physical stamina for participating in school sports
options.D: They teach her advanced management skills required for university entrance

explanation: Exactly. When too much housework is piled on a girl, she has little energy or time left for her books, homework, and rest. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h3)

question: How does community stigma directly affect the wellbeing of an HIV orphan?

options.A: It guarantees the child free medical care in local clinics
options.B: It forces the government to build private housing for them
options.C: It improves their academic performance through strict discipline
options.D: It leads to social rejection, bullying, and isolation

explanation: Stigma cuts children off from vital community support systems, worsening their emotional pain and loneliness. Your friendly smile can make a huge difference to a patient! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h4)

question: How do authorities decide if a substance is legally classified as hazardous waste?

options.A: By measuring how heavy the shipping container is when loaded onto a truck

options.C: By checking if the manufacturing company is publicly traded on the stock market
options.D: By looking at its specific waste stream source or dangerous characteristics

question: A nurse ignores a ward medication rule, and the patient gets hurt. What legal problem might this cause?

options.A: The hospital policy automatically protects the nurse from blame
options.B: The legal system ignores internal hospital rules completely
options.C: The policy becomes invalid because a nurse chose not to use it
options.D: The breach of policy can be used as evidence of negligence

question: What term describes paralysis that affects both legs and the lower half of the body?

question: What is the main risk of using a needle that is too short for an intramuscular injection?

options.A: The medicine will absorb too fast into the bloodstream
options.B: Medication enters the subcutaneous fat instead of muscle
options.C: The needle will bend or break inside the bone
options.D: Blood will flow backwards into the syringe instantly

question: What is the main goal of community health outreaches regarding self-medication?

options.A: Encouraging citizens to treat complex infections at home alone
options.B: Closing down all local patent medicine stores in rural towns
options.C: Educating the public on the dangers of unsupervised drug use
options.D: Selling cheap pharmaceutical products directly from hospital vans

explanation: Outreaches are all about grassroots education—helping everyday people understand why popping random pills without guidance can hurt them. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h7)

question: What makes a disaster different from a standard medical emergency?

options.A: An emergency never involves more than one healthcare provider.
options.B: An emergency only happens inside a hospital setting.
options.C: A disaster requires no coordination with outside agencies.
options.D: A disaster overwhelms local resources and involves mass casualties.

explanation: Spot on! While a normal emergency can be handled with the usual hospital staff and equipment, a disaster stretches everything past its breaking point because so many people are hurt at once. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h1)

question: In the famous 'four Ps' of labour, which one represents the 'Passenger'?

options.A: Uterine contractions
options.B: The fetus
options.C: The maternal pelvis
options.D: The mother's anxiety

question: As a nurse, what is your main goal when doing a risk assessment during antenatal care?

options.A: To accurately predict the exact day and hour of delivery
options.B: To eliminate the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: To detect potential complications early before they become life-threatening
options.D: To diagnose all genetic disorders in the unborn infant

explanation: Brilliant! Screening lets us spot moms who need extra support or specialized care early on, keeping both mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h7)

question: What makes communication in home health care different from a hospital setting?

options.A: Communication is restricted by hospital rules
options.B: Nurses rely solely on written medical charts
options.C: The nurse enters a private home as a guest
options.D: Patients have no family members present

explanation: Stepping into a patient's personal space completely changes the dynamic! Unlike a controlled clinic, you are a guest in their domain, which calls for extra respect and adaptability. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is the HbA1c test so helpful for managing diabetes over time?

options.A: It detects acute kidney failure caused by high blood sugar spikes

options.C: It evaluates the immediate effect of the patient's last meal on glucose

question: Why are small, frequent meals often recommended for patients with poor appetites?

options.A: They prevent the patient from feeling overwhelmed by large food portions.

options.C: They cure chronic digestive disorders within twenty-four hours.

explanation: Large meal trays often discourage weak or nauseated patients, whereas smaller portions look manageable and encourage better overall intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h8)

question: A patient arrives from a terrible car crash with massive internal bleeding. What must the trauma suite have ready immediately?

options.A: Cosmetic laser equipment and soothing music
options.B: Long-term recovery beds for overnight stays
options.C: Rapid blood transfusion equipment and crash carts
options.D: Specialized eye microscopes and micro-sutures

question: What is the main goal of 'deinstitutionalization' in mental health care?

options.A: Treating patients within local communities to maintain social ties
options.B: Closing all healthcare facilities to rely entirely on home remedies
options.C: Stopping the use of all medications for mental health conditions
options.D: Transferring all psychiatric patients to permanent prison cells

explanation: You got it! Deinstitutionalization simply means moving care out of big, isolated asylums and into local neighborhoods so patients can stay close to their families and support systems. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why must safety measures respect a patient's independence?

options.A: Patients will ignore rules that make them feel helpless
options.B: Families prefer not to assist elderly relatives
options.C: Independent patients recover faster from surgery
options.D: Hospital policies demand self-care routines

question: Why do nurses regularly monitor a child's growth?

options.A: To calculate exact adult height and weight
options.B: To diagnose specific genetic disorders instantly
options.C: To catch health and nutritional problems early
options.D: To replace routine medical checkups entirely

explanation: You've got this! Growth monitoring helps us spot tiny changes or downward trends early on, long before a child gets seriously ill. It's a quick win for preventive care! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h1)

question: How does knowing the exact physical boundaries of a community help you as a public health nurse?

options.A: It defines the specific population area where targeted health interventions are needed
options.B: It allows the nurse to purchase land for building a private pharmacy
options.C: It guarantees that all residents have equal access to clean drinking water
options.D: It prevents infectious diseases from spreading outside the neighborhood

explanation: Just like checking your landmark before crossing a street, knowing your boundaries helps you map your service area, track outbreaks, and make sure nobody gets left behind. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h2)

question: In which part of the female reproductive tract does fertilization usually take place?

options.B: Cervical canal
options.C: Ampulla of the fallopian tube
options.D: Ovarian cortex

question: What emotional state best describes the acceptance stage?

options.A: Intense bargaining for extra time with family
options.B: Extreme anger and hostility toward medical providers
options.C: Quiet peace and realistic acknowledgment of mortality
options.D: Joyful celebration of a long life well lived

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to use nystatin oral suspension for mouth thrush?

options.A: Swallow the liquid immediately on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
options.B: Swish the liquid thoroughly around the mouth before swallowing it
options.C: Dilute the entire bottle in a glass of cold fruit juice and drink it fast
options.D: Gargle the liquid at the back of the throat and spit it out without swallowing

question: Which antenatal practice helps prevent prolonged labour complications in our communities?

options.A: Identifying high-risk women and planning facility delivery
options.B: Relying entirely on home remedies for minor labour pains
options.C: Prescribing bed rest for all pregnant women after twenty weeks
options.D: Discouraging any form of physical activity throughout pregnancy

explanation: Excellent! Good antenatal screening lets us spot potential risks early so mothers can plan to deliver safely where expert help is available. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h7)

question: What are the small bumps on the surface of the tongue that house taste buds called?

options.A: Alveoli
options.B: Fauces
options.C: Uvula
options.D: Papillae

explanation: Papillae are the visible projections on the tongue surface that contain sensory receptors for taste. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is good room ventilation important when mixing or using strong chemical disinfectants?

options.A: To prevent dust particles from settling into open chemical buckets
options.B: To keep room temperatures low so the disinfectant does not freeze
options.C: To speed up the chemical drying time on large operating tables
options.D: To prevent toxic fumes from accumulating and causing respiratory irritation

explanation: Strong chemical vapors can hurt your lungs and throat if the room isn't well-aired out. Breathe easy by keeping windows or vents open! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h8)

question: How does a clinical ward nurse use epidemiological thinking during a shift?

options.A: By writing national health laws for the ministry of health
options.B: By performing complex statistical data entry for research journals
options.C: By noticing an increase in infections on the ward and looking for a common cause
options.D: By manufacturing new antibiotics in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Everyday nurses use mini-epidemiology all the time! Whenever you notice a sudden cluster of similar infections on your ward and start searching for the source, that's epidemiological thinking. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T1#GNS313_U1_T1_h5)

question: What usually happens in a ward that is poorly organized?

options.A: Doctors take over all daily medication administration tasks
options.B: Patient recovery times become much shorter automatically
options.C: Staff experience chaos and higher risks of clinical errors
options.D: Nurses have more time to spend on personal rest breaks

explanation: Spot on! When things lack structure, confusion creeps in, tasks get missed, and mistakes happen. Good organization keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a negative pressure isolation room?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Droplet precautions
options.D: Standard precautions

explanation: Negative pressure rooms prevent tiny airborne germs from drifting out into the hallway when the door is opened. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h4)

question: Which principle of primary health care ensures that vulnerable populations receive care regardless of wealth?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Centralization
options.C: Technological advancement
options.D: Specialization

explanation: Equity ensures fair distribution of health services so that vulnerable groups are not left behind. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h2)

question: Why is long-term intravenous therapy often administered via a PICC line for osteomyelitis patients?

options.A: It forces the antibiotic medication to bypass the stomach and land directly inside the infected bone cavity
options.B: It allows safe, long-term delivery of strong antibiotics directly into the bloodstream without frequent needle sticks
options.C: It prevents the patient from experiencing any side effects from the medication
options.D: It increases the white blood cell count within minutes of insertion

explanation: A PICC line provides reliable venous access for weeks of home or outpatient IV antibiotic therapy, sparing peripheral veins from damage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: What three categories are evaluated using the Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Heart rate, breathing rate, and blood pressure
options.B: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.C: Reflex speed, muscle tone, and pain tolerance
options.D: Cranial nerve integrity, balance, and coordination

explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale measures these three specific behavioral responses to quantify a patient's level of consciousness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h8)

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to need a surgical valve repair or replacement?

options.A: Simple ventricular ectopic beats
options.B: Severe aortic stenosis
options.C: Controlled essential hypertension
options.D: Mild sinus tachycardia

explanation: When a valve is severely narrowed (stenosis), blood can't get through properly. Surgery is often needed to fix or replace that physical blockage. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)

question: Which organ system takes over the final excretion of fetal nitrogenous wastes once they cross the placental membrane?

options.A: Fetal kidneys
options.B: Fetal liver
options.C: Maternal lungs
options.D: Maternal kidneys

explanation: Once urea and creatinine diffuse into the mother's blood, her kidneys filter them out and excrete them in her urine. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h6)

question: How should numbers inside a research table column normally be aligned?

options.A: To the right or by decimal points
options.B: Centered with uneven spacing
options.C: To the extreme left margin
options.D: Diagonally across the cells

explanation: Right-aligning or lining up numbers by their decimal points makes it super easy to compare sizes up and down at a glance. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h4)

question: What does a simple frequency distribution table show us?

options.A: A map of hospital departments
options.B: The exact daily schedule of clinical staff
options.C: The financial budget of a hospital ward
options.D: How often specific values or categories occur

explanation: A frequency table simply counts and shows how many times a particular observation or response pops up in your data. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h3)

question: What usually happens to a patient's pulse rate when their body temperature goes up?

options.A: The heart rate goes down
options.B: The pulse becomes weak and irregular
options.C: The heart rate stays completely normal
options.D: The heart rate goes up

explanation: Correct! As body temperature climbs, the metabolism speeds up, making the heart beat faster too. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T6#GNS123_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of teaching communities about infection control?

options.A: To empower patients with practical knowledge to protect themselves
options.B: To eliminate all microorganisms from the environment
options.C: To replace the need for professional medical diagnosis
options.D: To ensure patients never leave their homes

explanation: Knowledge is power! When we educate our communities, we give people the tools to keep themselves and their families safe. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T11#GNS313_U2_T11_h7)

question: Which layer of the hydatid cyst makes the fluid and new parasite cells?

options.A: Epicyst
options.B: Ectocyst
options.C: Endocyst
options.D: Pericyst

explanation: The inner layer, called the endocyst, is the active part that produces fluid and new cyst parts. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h4)

question: What standard p-value do nursing researchers usually look for to prove statistical significance?
explanation: 0.05 is the gold standard in research! It tells us there's a 5% or lower chance our results happened purely by random luck. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h6)

question: A pregnant patient refuses to eat eggs due to a local tradition. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Ignore the dietary restriction since culture has no impact on health.
options.B: Scold the family for holding backward customs that harm their health.
options.C: Acknowledge her belief respectfully while discussing alternative local foods that provide the same nutrients.
options.D: Force the patient to eat eggs during her hospital admission.

explanation: Brilliant nursing judgment! Great care means respecting a patient's culture while gently finding safe, alternative ways to meet their nutritional needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h4)

question: What happens to the spread of disease if a nurse successfully breaks even one link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless bacteria
options.B: The patient develops instant immunity against all other germs
options.C: The infection cycle is stopped and disease spread is prevented
options.D: The reservoir completely disappears from the environment

explanation: Because the chain requires every single link to function, breaking just one link halts the entire transmission process. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

options.A: Generate fast electrical impulses for muscle movement
options.B: Fight off bacterial infections in the bloodstream
options.C: Digest food particles inside the stomach lumen
options.D: Act as chemical messengers to regulate body functions

explanation: Think of hormones as the body's postal service! They are chemical messengers sent out by glands to travel through the blood and help manage how different organs work. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T10#GNS211_U1_T10_h1)

question: A client comes to the clinic reporting pus, warmth, and increasing redness around her implant site five days after placement. What should you suspect?

options.A: A localized site infection requiring prompt medical evaluation and treatment
options.B: A sign that the implant has expired and needs immediate replacement
options.C: A normal healing reaction that proves the hormone is working effectively
options.D: A standard allergic reaction to the pressure bandage adhesive tape

explanation: Pus, warmth, and spreading redness are classic signs of a minor wound infection. It's nothing to panic about, but it definitely needs prompt cleaning and medical care! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h8)

question: What does the word 'palsy' mean in relation to cerebral palsy?

options.A: Infection of the spinal cord
options.B: A sudden loss of consciousness
options.C: Weakness or problems using muscles
options.D: Gradual shrinking of the brain

explanation: Palsy specifically refers to a lack of muscle control or weakness that interferes with normal movement. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h1)

question: A patient is going home soon but needs a hospital bed and oxygen set up at their house. Who usually arranges this?

options.A: The case manager
options.B: The staff speech therapist
options.C: The physical therapist
options.D: The attending physiatrist

explanation: Case managers are logistics pros! They handle discharge planning to ensure all necessary medical equipment is ready at home before the patient leaves. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h6)

question: According to the World Health Organization, true health is much more than just not being sick. What else does it include?

options.A: It includes complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: It requires regular laboratory blood test monitoring
options.C: It focuses primarily on the absence of chronic illness
options.D: It measures physical endurance and athletic capacity

explanation: Think about it like this: a person might be free from disease, but if they are stressed mentally or struggling socially, they aren't fully healthy yet. Health is the whole package! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is venepuncture primarily used for in clinical practice?

options.A: Withdrawing blood for diagnostic testing
options.B: Checking lung function capacity
options.C: Assessing electrical heart activity
options.D: Measuring deep body temperature

explanation: Venepuncture involves piercing a vein to collect blood samples needed for various laboratory investigations. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h1)

question: What does the handy acronym IMRAD stand for in research writing?

options.A: Introduction, Management, Results, and Documentation
options.B: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion
options.C: Investigation, Materials, Review, and Data
options.D: Information, Measurement, Reporting, and Analysis

explanation: IMRAD is just a simple roadmap researchers use to organize their papers. Once you know it, reading studies becomes super easy! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient has a high fever and flushed, warm skin. Which process is the body using to cool down?

options.A: Vasoconstriction and shivering
options.B: Vasodilation and sweating
options.C: Keratin buildup and cell shedding
options.D: Fat storage and hair growth

explanation: The body responds to high heat by widening blood vessels and producing sweat to promote heat loss. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which statement describes a study with good external validity?

options.A: The measurement tool produced the exact same score on repeated testing
options.B: The researchers strictly controlled all extraneous variables in the lab
options.C: The sample size was large enough to calculate a valid percentage
options.D: The results can be safely generalized to patients in other healthcare settings

explanation: Think of external validity as your study's passport—it means the findings can travel out of the lab and apply to real patients elsewhere. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h6)

question: A new mother on the ward is bleeding heavily two hours after delivery, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Eclamptic seizure
options.B: Obstructed labor
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Uterine atony

explanation: When the uterus fails to contract firmly (atony), the blood vessels stay open and bleeding happens. A firm massage and oxytocics are usually our best friends here! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T013#GNS226_U1_T013_h3)

question: A nurse uses a stethoscope to listen to bowel sounds after surgery. Which method of acquiring knowledge is this?

options.A: Rational method
options.B: Method of tenacity
options.C: Empirical method
options.D: Method of authority

explanation: Listening with a stethoscope is a direct sensory observation, which is the exact definition of the empirical method. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h6)

question: What should you do if a patient cannot remember the names of their home medications?

options.A: Disregard home drugs and start fresh hospital drugs
options.B: Guess the medications based on their visible disease symptoms
options.C: Scold the patient for being careless with their health
options.D: Ask the patient or family to bring all medicine containers to the clinic

explanation: Having them bring their actual bottles or sachets gives you exact, reliable data when memory fails. Simple and practical! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main difference between delirium and dementia?

options.A: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating change in mental status
options.B: Dementia can be completely cured with antibiotics
options.C: Dementia causes sudden hallucinations without memory loss
options.D: Delirium develops gradually over several years

explanation: Spot on! Delirium comes on suddenly (often because of an infection or illness) and changes throughout the day. Dementia is a slow, long-term decline in memory and thinking. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h4)

question: What are the two big features that define all stem cells?

options.A: Programmed death and shrinkage
options.B: Rapid mutation and anaplasia
options.C: Self-renewal and potency
options.D: Encapsulation and metastasis

explanation: Spot on! Stem cells are amazing because they can both make copies of themselves (self-renewal) and turn into specialized cells (potency). [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why should a quality improvement team always include someone working right on the hospital floor?

options.A: To secure funding grants for new medical equipment purchases
options.B: To handle all communication with hospital executive management
options.C: To replace the team leader when meetings run too late
options.D: To provide real-world feedback on how changes affect daily workflow

explanation: Spot on! Frontline staff make sure that new ideas are actually realistic and practical for the nurses and aides doing the work every day. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h2)

question: What classic mix of symptoms do you expect to see in an opioid overdose?

options.A: Rapid heart rate, muscle tremors, and agitation
options.B: Profuse sweating, diarrhea, and high blood pressure
options.C: High fever, dry skin, and wide pupils
options.D: Slow breathing, extreme sleepiness, and pinpoint pupils

explanation: Picture a sleeping patient who is breathing very slowly with tiny, pin-point pupils—that's the classic classic opioid sign you'll learn to spot instantly! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h5)

question: Where is the pons located relative to the medulla oblongata?

options.A: Lateral
options.B: Inferior
options.C: Superior
options.D: Anterior

explanation: The pons sits directly above (superior to) the medulla oblongata on the brainstem. Think of it as stepping up one level! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h1)

question: A nurse is teaching range-of-motion exercises to a patient recovering from a stroke. Which level of prevention is this?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Rehabilitation and preventing further disability from an established disease fall under tertiary prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h3)

question: In conductive hearing loss, what is the main issue preventing sound from being heard clearly?

options.A: Hair cells inside the cochlea are permanently destroyed
options.B: The auditory nerve is completely severed from the brain
options.C: Sound waves are blocked from reaching the inner ear
options.D: Electrical signals bypass the brain's temporal lobe

explanation: You've got this! Conductive hearing loss simply means something is blocking sound waves from traveling through the outer or middle ear. Think of it like a blocked pathway. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h1)

question: If local stores see a drop in meat sales and a huge spike in cheap instant noodles, what does this usually tell us?

options.A: Improved local agricultural output of grain-based factory foods
options.B: An unexpected surplus of manufacturing capacity for wheat products
options.C: A sudden cultural shift favoring processed instant meals over cooking
options.D: Decreased household purchasing power altering dietary choices

explanation: When people have less money, they buy cheaper comfort foods, changing their overall diet quality. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h3)

question: What is your absolute first priority if you notice a patient is experiencing harm during care?

options.A: Completing the administrative paperwork for insurance claims
options.B: Notifying the hospital legal team before touching the patient
options.C: Interviewing witnesses to determine who made the mistake
options.D: Stabilizing the patient and halting any ongoing harmful intervention

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the patient safe and stable always comes first, which means stopping whatever is causing harm right away before anything else. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h6)

question: When should you release the pulled skin tissue when doing a Z-track injection?

options.A: Immediately before pushing the plunger down
options.B: Before cleansing the skin site with an alcohol swab
options.C: After the needle has been completely withdrawn
options.D: While the needle is still inside the muscle tissue

explanation: Keep holding that skin until the needle is completely out! Letting go only after the needle is gone ensures the track zips shut and traps the medicine inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: A nurse only checks clinic records to decide what health program to build. What is the biggest downside to this?

options.A: It is too expensive for hospital computers
options.B: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions
options.C: It takes too many years to gather basic stats
options.D: It misses vulnerable people who never make it to the clinic

explanation: You got it! Clinic records only show those who could reach the facility. You might completely miss sick people who are too far away or can't afford transport. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h3)

question: What does a high dependency ratio mean for a country?

options.A: Every citizen is completely financially independent.
options.B: The government has excess funds for infrastructure projects.
options.C: A small working-age population must support a large number of dependents.
options.D: There are more elderly people than working adults.

explanation: A high dependency ratio means fewer working adults are carrying the financial weight of supporting a large group of children and elderly dependents. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h5)

question: Which model explains that people change their habits by moving through steps like thinking about it, and then finally taking action?

options.A: The Biomedical Treatment Model
options.B: The Environmental Sanitation Grid
options.C: The Germ Theory of Disease
options.D: The Transtheoretical Model

explanation: Well done! The Transtheoretical Model breaks down the journey of change from early thoughts all the way to long-term maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h2)

question: What does a normal P wave tell us on an ECG?

options.A: Sudden failure of the aortic valve
options.B: Electrical activation of the atria
options.C: Complete relaxation of the whole heart
options.D: Dangerous blockage in a coronary artery

explanation: The little P wave is just the atria waking up and squeezing blood down to the ventricles. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T16#GNS213_U1_T16_h4)

question: Why do nurses check sensation across different skin areas when assessing a patient with a back injury?

options.A: To measure the amount of cerebrospinal fluid surrounding the cord
options.B: To check if the patient's blood pressure is stable
options.C: To map out dermatomes and identify the exact spinal level of injury
options.D: To stimulate voluntary movement in the paralyzed limbs

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! By testing where the patient can or cannot feel touch, you can map the dermatomes and pinpoint exactly which part of the spine is damaged. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T24#GNS211_U3_T24_h5)

question: When should you close, seal, and replace a sharps container?

options.A: Only when it is completely overflowing to save space
options.B: Whenever the outside gets a bit dusty
options.C: When it is about three-quarters full
options.D: At the very end of every month, no matter what

explanation: Safety first! Stopping at three-quarters full prevents people from trying to force more items in and accidentally getting a needle-stick injury. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h4)

question: During which procedure is the lithotomy position most commonly used?

options.A: Feeding a patient with dysphagia
options.B: Listening to breath sounds in asthma
options.C: Gynecological examinations and childbirth
options.D: Administering a nebulizer treatment

explanation: Lithotomy has the patient on their back with feet up in stirrups, perfect for pelvic checks and welcoming new babies! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h6)

question: If someone accidentally gets a corrosive chemical in their eyes or on their skin, what is the recommended minimum time to flush it with clean water?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 15 minutes
options.C: Until the burning stops
options.D: One full hour

explanation: You nailed it! Flushing continuously for at least 15 minutes is crucial to dilute the chemical and wash it away before it burns deep into the tissue. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h6)

question: Once Luteinizing Hormone (LH) finally reaches the gonads, what is its main job?

options.A: It lowers overall body temperature
options.B: It stimulates sex steroid production
options.C: It stops the secretion of GnRH
options.D: It triggers immediate linear height growth

explanation: Spot on! LH targets specific cells in the gonads to prompt the creation of powerhouse sex hormones like testosterone and estrogen. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main reason for doing regular physical stock counts in a pharmacy?

options.A: To compare actual pills on the shelf with recorded ledger numbers
options.B: To calculate the annual bonus for the hospital accountant
options.C: To make the pharmacy staff work longer hours on the weekend
options.D: To dispose of all medications that have been on the shelf for one week

explanation: Counting actual stock helps catch issues like missing items, breakage, or recording mistakes early. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when helping someone with a fresh thermal burn?

options.A: Apply antibiotic ointment to prevent infection
options.B: Apply ice packs directly to the wound to reduce swelling
options.C: Stop the burning process and apply cool water
options.D: Scrub the burn vigorously with antiseptic soap

explanation: Always stop the burning first and cool it with clean running water! Never use ice, though—it causes blood vessels to clamp down and makes the injury worse. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why might a rural village suddenly see vitamin deficiencies during the heavy rainy season?

options.A: Excessive rainfall causing an overabundance of fresh meat in local stores
options.B: Villagers deliberately choosing to fast from fruits and vegetables during rainstorms
options.C: Washed-out roads cutting off transport of fresh produce from regional markets
options.D: Soil contamination making all locally grown crops completely poisonous

explanation: Bad weather washes out roads, isolating communities so fresh, perishable foods can't get delivered. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T027#GNS227_U2_T027_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of patient safety in healthcare?

options.A: Speeding up patient discharge times
options.B: Reducing the number of hired staff
options.C: Eliminating all hospital financial costs
options.D: Preventing unintended harm during care

explanation: Patient safety focuses directly on avoiding and preventing any accidental injury or harm to individuals while they are receiving medical treatment. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main job of target cell receptors in the endocrine system?

options.A: To recognize and securely bind to specific circulating hormones
options.B: To destroy excess hormones before they reach the bloodstream
options.C: To filter metabolic waste products out of cellular tissue
options.D: To manufacture new cholesterol for hormone production

explanation: Think of receptors as custom locks, and hormones as the matching keys. They ensure that only the right message triggers the right cell! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h4)

question: A new mother has a tear involving her perineal muscles, but her anal sphincter is completely untouched. What kind of tear is this?

options.A: Third-degree tear
options.B: Second-degree tear
options.C: Fourth-degree tear
options.D: First-degree tear

explanation: When a tear goes deeper into the perineal muscles but stops before reaching the anal sphincter, we classify it as a second-degree tear. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of tilting the X-ray table into different angles during a barium swallow?

options.A: To drain excess stomach fluids before the contrast is given
options.B: To help gravity coat the entire lining of the esophagus and stomach with barium
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the procedure
options.D: To speed up the digestion of the barium into the bloodstream

explanation: Changing table positions ensures that the liquid barium flows over all mucosal surfaces so small defects or ulcers are not missed. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why is it helpful to involve traditional and religious leaders in community health strategies?

options.A: They hold strong influence over community attitudes and can help promote health-seeking behaviors
options.B: They can write legal prescriptions for controlled narcotic medications
options.C: They control the central government budget for foreign medical equipment
options.D: They are legally trained to replace licensed medical doctors in emergency surgery

explanation: Brilliant! Local leaders are deeply respected; partnering with them helps clear up cultural myths and encourages community members to embrace healthcare. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is giving large volumes of IV fluids dangerous for a patient in cardiogenic shock?

options.A: It causes an immediate drop in body temperature and shivering
options.B: It dissolves blood clots in the coronary arteries too fast
options.C: It triggers a severe allergic reaction in the blood vessels
options.D: It worsens heart failure by overloading a weak heart that cannot pump the fluid

explanation: A failing heart cannot handle extra fluid volume, which leads to fluid backing up into the lungs and worsening respiratory failure. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to know the difference between civil and criminal law?

options.A: To write new hospital policies for the intensive care unit
options.B: To know which court actions can result from clinical mistakes
options.C: To prosecute patients who refuse to take their oral medications
options.D: To replace the hospital legal team during a malpractice suit

explanation: As a nurse, knowing your legal boundaries keeps you safe. You need to understand how different legal actions apply if something goes wrong in practice. [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h1)

question: Why does blood suddenly rush into a newborn's lungs right after their very first breath?

options.A: The heart rate increases rapidly
options.B: Umbilical cord clamping increases volume
options.C: Pulmonary vascular resistance drops
options.D: Systemic blood pressure decreases

explanation: When the baby takes that first breath and air fills the lungs, the blood vessels inside open right up, letting blood rush in easily to pick up oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h1)

question: Why do bedside nurses need to know a little bit about hospital finances?

options.A: Every hospital supply and shift hour costs money
options.B: It allows nurses to purchase private equipment for their wards
options.C: Clinical outcomes have no relation to operational budgets
options.D: Nurses are legally required to manage the hospital bank accounts

explanation: Everyday choices on the ward—like how we use supplies or schedule shifts—directly affect the hospital's budget. Great nurses care for both patients and resources! [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h1)

question: What happens to fixed costs when patient numbers go up in the hospital?

options.A: They stay exactly the same
options.B: They become direct costs
options.C: They increase significantly
options.D: They drop down to zero

explanation: Fixed costs (like building rent) don't care how many patients walk through the door; they stay stubborn and unchanging regardless! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do health teams check 'signal functions' instead of just looking at hospital buildings?

options.A: To verify that actual life-saving treatments are actively being delivered to patients
options.B: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of hospital lighting
options.C: To determine the architectural layout required for nursing stations
options.D: To audit the daily cleaning schedules of delivery rooms

explanation: A nice building isn't enough! Signal functions prove that the staff, drugs, and equipment are actually there to save lives. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h4)

question: What often causes the biggest hurdles for people with physical disabilities in daily life?

options.A: Inaccessible physical environments and negative social attitudes
options.B: A lack of interest in attending family social gatherings
options.C: The mandatory use of modern assistive walking frames
options.D: Excessive consumption of prescribed rehabilitation vitamins

explanation: Often, bad societal attitudes and buildings without ramps or lifts cause more barriers than the physical condition itself. We must be change agents! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h9)

question: What does opt-out HIV testing mean during antenatal care?

options.A: The test is performed routinely unless the woman explicitly refuses it.
options.B: Only women with visible clinical symptoms are required to take the test.
options.C: The husband must give written consent before the wife can be tested.
options.D: Testing is completely optional and only done if the patient asks for it.

explanation: Opt-out screening means HIV testing is automatically included in routine prenatal lab work, and patients must actively decline if they do not want it. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h4)

question: Why must a nurse use a separate measuring cylinder for each patient when emptying drainage bags?

options.A: To stop the plastic containers from wearing out too quickly
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination and spread of infections between patients
options.C: To make measuring the fluid much faster during busy shifts
options.D: To ensure the hospital records look neat and well-organized

explanation: Infection control 101! Using dedicated equipment for every patient keeps germs from hitching a ride across the ward. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T22#GNS212_U1_T22_h5)

question: Which main muscle forms the wall of the urinary bladder and stretches as it fills up with urine?

options.A: Trigone muscle
options.B: Detrusor muscle
options.C: Dartos muscle
options.D: Cremaster muscle

explanation: You've got this! The detrusor muscle is the big muscular wall of the bladder that stretches out nicely to hold urine until you're ready to go. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h1)

question: When making the initial cut to drain an abscess, which direction should the surgical blade follow?

options.A: Directly perpendicular to muscle fibers
options.B: In a randomized zigzag pattern
options.C: Along the natural skin tension lines
options.D: In a wide circular shape around the border

explanation: Cutting along the body's natural skin lines (Langer's lines) helps the wound heal better and keeps scarring to a minimum. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h4)

question: A patient asks why her injectable birth control takes months to wear off after her scheduled date. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The medicine travels directly to the brain and stays in the neurons
options.B: The injection forms a slow-release depot store in the muscle tissue
options.C: The drug permanently alters the DNA structure of the ovaries
options.D: The liver stores the chemical in fat cells for future energy use

explanation: Injectables like DMPA are designed as a "depot" injection, meaning the muscle holds onto the medicine and releases it slowly into the body over a few months. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h3)

question: What is the very first step when you want to start a nursing research project?

options.A: Applying for hospital funding
options.B: Collecting patient blood samples
options.C: Identifying the research problem
options.D: Writing the final conclusion

explanation: Every good study starts by figuring out what the exact problem is. You have to spot the gap in patient care before you can start gathering any data! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h1)

question: What jelly-like structure in the inner ear gets pushed when moving fluid hits it during a head turn?

options.A: Otolith
options.B: Cupula
options.C: Tectorial membrane
options.D: Macula

explanation: The cupula acts just like a tiny swinging door inside your ear, moving whenever the fluid pushes against it. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h3)

question: How do corrosive chemical substances mainly damage human tissue?

options.A: By triggering sudden allergic respiratory attacks
options.B: By altering genetic DNA over many decades
options.C: By depressing the central nervous system through inhalation
options.D: By destroying living tissue upon direct physical contact

explanation: Think of strong acids or bases—when they touch your skin or mucous membranes, they cause immediate, visible chemical damage right on the spot! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why do important minerals like iron and calcium need active transport to cross the placenta?

options.A: They can only travel when the mother's heart rate is very high
options.B: They are too large to pass through any membrane without being broken down
options.C: They dissolve directly into the amniotic fluid instead of fetal blood
options.D: They are moved against a concentration gradient to ensure the fetus gets enough

explanation: Active transport means the placenta uses energy to pump these minerals in—even if the baby already has more of them than the mother does! Nature makes sure the baby gets what it needs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h5)

question: How does the respiratory system respond if blood pH drops and the body becomes too acidic?

options.A: Decreases the rate and depth of breathing
options.B: Increases the rate and depth of breathing
options.C: Stops breathing completely for short intervals
options.D: Retains all available oxygen in the alveoli

explanation: When blood is too acidic, you breathe faster and deeper to blow off excess carbon dioxide ($CO_2$). Since $CO_2$ acts as an acid, getting rid of it raises the pH back up! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h4)

question: In community health statistics, what does 'incidence' tell us?

options.A: The total number of all old and new cases in a population
options.B: The percentage of infected patients who die from the disease
options.C: The number of new cases of a disease over a specific time
options.D: The expected baseline level of an illness in a community

explanation: Think of incidence as new arrivals! It counts brand-new cases popping up so nurses can see how fast an illness is currently spreading. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is teaching a patient to keep a menstrual calendar a helpful nursing action?

options.A: It replaces the need for any further laboratory blood testing
options.B: It serves as a permanent medical cure for abnormal hormones
options.C: It completely prevents the future development of ovarian cysts
options.D: It empowers the patient to track cycle patterns and share accurate data with clinicians

explanation: Data is power! A calendar helps both the nurse and the patient see patterns clearly, spot changes early, and check if treatments are working. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing duty during a poisoning emergency?

options.A: Collecting and labeling biological samples for analysis
options.B: Synthesizing new chemical antidotes in the hospital pharmacy
options.C: Ensuring personal protective equipment is worn correctly
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and watching for sudden clinical changes

explanation: Nurses monitor patients, use safety gear, and collect labs, but we leave the chemical manufacturing to the pharmacists! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T1#GNS215_U5_T1_h6)

question: What tool do public health officials mainly use to track FGM rates across Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Customs Import Records
options.B: Primary School Attendance Sheets
options.C: Demographic and Health Surveys
options.D: National Electoral Voting Registers

explanation: Correct! Health surveys give us reliable statistical data on how common FGM is and how trends are shifting across different regions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h8)

question: Which layer of the pleura hugs the outer surface of the lungs tightly?

options.A: Mediastinal pleura
options.B: Parietal pleura
options.C: Diaphragmatic pleura
options.D: Visceral pleura

explanation: You've got this! Think of the visceral pleura as the inner skin that sticks right onto the lung tissue. Great job keeping up with your anatomy! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T7#GNS213_U2_T7_h1)

question: What change in vital signs do you commonly notice in a physically distressed mum?

options.A: Fast heart rate and rapid breathing
options.B: High and bounding pulse pressure
options.C: Very low body temperature
options.D: Slow, shallow respiratory rate

explanation: That adrenaline rush speeds everything up! You'll often spot a racing heart (tachycardia) and quick, shallow breathing (tachypnea). [learn more](GNS226_U4_T002#GNS226_U4_T002_h4)

question: Why do patients taking anticholinergics often end up with constipation?

options.A: Abdominal muscles become paralyzed by the drug
options.B: The medication slows down gastrointestinal motility
options.C: The drug pulls water directly out of the stool
options.D: Bile production in the liver is completely stopped

explanation: Just like it slows down the bladder, the drug also slows down movement in the gut. Less movement means sluggish bowels! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h5)

question: Which major brain relay station do smell signals skip completely?

options.A: Brainstem
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Medulla
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: Brilliant! While sight, hearing, and touch all route through the thalamus first, your sense of smell takes a VIP shortcut straight to the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T9#GNS211_U4_T9_h5)

question: Why do medications absorb very slowly from the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: The epidermis blocks most medications from entering.
options.B: Sweat glands actively wash the medication away.
options.C: Skin cells in the dermis are tightly packed together.
options.D: The dermis has a very limited blood supply.

explanation: Limited blood vessels in the dermis mean the drug stays localized and is picked up very gradually by the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: What do we mean by Post-Ebola Syndrome?

options.A: A collection of chronic physical symptoms persisting after recovery
options.B: A permanent mental illness from the incubation period
options.C: An acute respiratory infection before fever starts
options.D: A sudden relapse of active internal bleeding on day two

explanation: You got it! Even after beating the virus, survivors can deal with lingering joint pain, fatigue, and vision issues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is the main difference between problem-focused and emotion-focused coping?

options.A: Emotion-focused fixes physical organs, while problem-focused cures mental illness
options.B: Problem-focused is always unhealthy, while emotion-focused is always beneficial
options.C: Problem-focused involves denial, while emotion-focused involves physical exercise
options.D: Problem-focused deals with the actual stressor, while emotion-focused manages feelings about it

explanation: Problem-focused coping targets the root cause of stress, whereas emotion-focused coping helps soothe the emotional distress caused by the situation. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do the bars in a histogram touch each other with no gaps?

options.A: To represent separate categorical nursing shifts
options.B: To show that the underlying data is continuous
options.C: To save space on the research paper page
options.D: To hide missing data points from the reader

explanation: Since the numbers flow smoothly from one value to the next without breaks, the bars stick together to show that flow! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T9#GNS217_U4_T9_h2)

question: How fast do chemical buffer systems jump into action when blood pH changes?

options.A: Within fractions of a second
options.B: Over three to five days
options.C: Only when stimulated by the kidneys
options.D: After several hours

explanation: Chemical buffers are the body's fastest responders. They react almost instantly to catch sudden pH changes before other organs even start working. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h3)

question: What is the main job of active vitamin D once processed by the kidneys?

options.A: To lower blood pressure by widening blood vessels
options.B: To speed up the filtration rate of the glomerulus
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in marrow
options.D: To promote calcium and phosphorus absorption in the gut

explanation: Spot on! Active vitamin D helps your intestines absorb calcium and phosphorus from your food so your body has what it needs for strong bones. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why does damage to the pancreas often lead to both digestive problems and blood sugar issues?

options.A: Digestive enzymes and hormones are stored inside the exact same cells.
options.B: Insulin is required to activate all major pancreatic digestive enzymes.
options.C: The pancreas has both exocrine and endocrine functions in one organ.
options.D: The pancreas shares a direct blood supply with the liver and stomach.

explanation: You've got this! The pancreas is a multitasker. It acts as an exocrine gland to help us digest food, and an endocrine gland to manage our blood sugar. When it gets injured, both jobs take a hit. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h1)

question: How does actively absorbing sodium from the gut affect fluid movement?

options.A: It destroys water molecules to prevent severe dehydration
options.B: It draws water out of the lumen and into the mucosal cells
options.C: It repels water molecules and forces them into the stool
options.D: It keeps water trapped inside the lumen until digestion finishes

explanation: Exactly! Pumping sodium out of the gut space creates an osmotic pull that drags water right along with it into the body tissues. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T012#GNS227_U1_T012_h6)

question: How do selective media help microbiologists isolate specific microorganisms?

options.A: By changing color every time a fungus touches the plate
options.B: By destroying all living cells present in a water sample
options.C: By allowing certain microbes to grow while stopping the growth of others
options.D: By keeping the Petri dish completely sterile without a lid

explanation: Spot on! Selective media contain special ingredients that block unwanted bacteria so only the specific germ you are looking for can multiply. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h4)

question: A Nigerian dietitian is counseling a patient with high blood pressure who has a modest income. What is the most practical advice?

options.A: Recommend affordable local foods and suggest low-salt preparation methods
options.B: Tell the patient to rely entirely on hospital meal deliveries
options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating all local carbohydrates completely
options.D: Prescribe expensive imported supplements available only online

explanation: Spot on! Good counseling must fit the patient's pocket. It's always best to recommend healthy, accessible local foods prepared with less salt. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h6)

question: What is a quick, drug-free comfort measure you can teach a patient for crampy pelvic pain?

options.A: Engaging in high-intensity aerobic exercise
options.B: Consuming high amounts of caffeine
options.C: Applying ice packs directly to the pelvic region
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

explanation: A simple hot water bottle or heating pad works wonders by relaxing tense pelvic muscles and easing nasty cramps. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T21#GNS216_U5_T21_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way for a visually impaired patient to tell different medicine bottles apart?

options.A: Using distinct physical shapes or textured bumps on bottle caps
options.B: Asking a trusted family member to organize and label the medications
options.C: Reading the standard small-print label by dim bedside candlelight
options.D: Placing tactile rubber bands around specific prescription containers

explanation: Trying to read tiny print in dim light is a recipe for a medication error if you have low vision! Using touch-based methods like rubber bands or textured caps is much safer. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T9#GNS311_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a reliable way for a nurse to check if a patient is really taking their drugs?

options.A: Conducting pill counts and reviewing pharmacy refill logs
options.B: Trusting that the patient remembers all dosing schedules accurately
options.C: Assuming compliance if the patient smiles during clinic visits
options.D: Asking family members if they think the patient looks healthy

explanation: Numbers don't lie! Pill counts and pharmacy records give us solid proof of whether the medicine is actually leaving the container. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which specific viral infection is the primary cause of almost all cervical cancer cases?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.C: Hepatitis B virus
options.D: Herpes simplex virus

explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) strains is recognized as the necessary causal agent for the development of cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h2)

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain?

options.A: 31 pairs
options.B: 24 pairs
options.C: 12 pairs
options.D: 8 pairs

explanation: There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves that connect the brain directly to various structures mostly located in the head and neck. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers say the line between 'natural' and 'man-made' disasters is often blurry?

options.A: Technological failures always trigger weather events
options.B: Governments hide the true cause of every emergency
options.C: Natural disasters only happen where humans live
options.D: Human actions often make natural hazards much worse

explanation: Things like cutting down trees or poor town planning can make a flood or storm way more damaging than it should be. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the epiglottis during swallowing?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of incoming swallowed liquids
options.B: Produce saliva to break down solid food particles
options.C: Pump air directly into the upper respiratory tract
options.D: Cover the larynx to direct food into the esophagus

explanation: The epiglottis acts as a protective lid that folds over the windpipe when we swallow, keeping food out of the airway. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h1)

question: If a needle is missing after a big surgery, what is the next step the team should take?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy if the patient looks stable
options.B: Assume the needle evaporated and finish stitching the skin
options.C: Ask the patient to pay for a replacement needle
options.D: Perform a thorough search of the room and take an X-ray

explanation: Spot on! A missing needle means a full search of the room and an X-ray to confirm where it went. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is the standard normal fasting blood sugar range for a healthy adult?

options.A: Below 100 mg/dL
options.B: 140 to 180 mg/dL
options.C: 200 to 250 mg/dL
options.D: Above 300 mg/dL

explanation: A fasting blood sugar reading under 100 mg/dL is considered normal for individuals without metabolic disorders. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h6)
