question: Why is assessment in palliative care an ongoing cycle rather than a one-time thing?

options.A: Hospital policies require daily paperwork updates from the nursing staff
options.B: Patient conditions and symptoms shift as the illness progresses
options.C: Insurance companies demand new symptom scores before paying bills
options.D: Doctors change their minds about medications every few hours

explanation: Because serious illnesses change rapidly, as nurses we need to keep checking in so we can catch new discomforts early. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the best way to help a patient stick to their long-term blood pressure medication plan?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop taking pills whenever their blood pressure normalizes
options.B: Explaining that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it
options.C: Insisting that family members administer every daily dose orally
options.D: Warning the patient that stopping pills causes instant cardiac arrest

explanation: Fantastic! Patients often stop taking meds when they feel fine. Teaching them that the drugs are keeping their pressure under control helps them stay consistent for life. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T2#GNS223_U1_T2_h8)

question: How does regular physical activity benefit a patient with Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: It helps body cells respond better to available insulin
options.B: It allows the patient to eat unlimited amounts of sugar
options.C: It permanently repairs destroyed cells inside the pancreas
options.D: It replaces the daily need for checking blood sugar levels

explanation: Exercise makes muscle and tissue cells more sensitive to insulin, allowing glucose to move out of the blood and into cells more easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: Which hormone is the main one responsible for lowering your blood sugar after you eat a meal?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Adrenaline

explanation: Spot on! Insulin is released by your pancreas to help glucose move out of your bloodstream and into your body cells to give you energy. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h1)

question: What does your body do with extra carbohydrates when you eat more than you immediately need?

options.A: It converts all excess carbohydrates directly into bone tissue.
options.B: It eliminates them completely through the urinary system.
options.C: It stores the extra fuel as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
options.D: It turns them into water molecules to hydrate the cells.

explanation: Nothing goes to waste! When you have extra energy, your body packs it away neatly as glycogen in your liver and muscles for later use. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h2)

question: Which type of validity involves checking if a new tool compares well with an established gold standard?

options.A: Surface validity
options.B: Criterion validity
options.C: Face validity
options.D: Content validity

explanation: Criterion validity is established when a new instrument scores similarly to a trusted, proven gold-standard tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which bacterium causes General Paralysis of the Insane (GPI)?

options.A: Neisseria meningitidis
options.B: Treponema pallidum
options.C: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae

explanation: You got this! GPI is a serious neurological condition that happens when a syphilis infection caused by Treponema pallidum is left untreated for a long time. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h1)

question: A patient calls two days after an abortion saying she is soaking through three large pads every hour. What should you tell her?

options.A: Reassure her that heavy bleeding lasts a whole month
options.B: Tell her it is normal and to call back next week
options.C: Take extra birth control pills to slow down the flow
options.D: Come to the clinic or emergency department right away

explanation: Soaking more than two pads an hour for two hours is a major red flag for heavy bleeding. She needs medical attention urgently! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h7)

question: As a nurse, what is your most critical intervention to catch energy imbalances early in hospitalized patients?

options.A: Restricting family visits during meals
options.B: Performing regular and accurate weight measurements
options.C: Asking the patient their favorite food
options.D: Administering a daily multivitamin

explanation: You've got this! Tracking weight trends over time is the most reliable way for a nurse to see if a patient's calorie intake is matching what their body needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h8)

question: How long does morning stiffness typically last for someone with osteoarthritis?

options.A: Only occurring late at night
options.B: Less than thirty minutes
options.C: Several hours throughout the day
options.D: All day without any relief

explanation: Correct! OA morning stiffness is usually brief—lasting under thirty minutes—which helps doctors tell it apart from other inflammatory joint problems. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h3)

question: Which dimension of holistic care involves a person's sense of meaning, purpose, and faith?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Physical dimension
options.C: Social dimension
options.D: Mental dimension

explanation: The spiritual dimension connects a patient to their core values, life purpose, and faith traditions. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must you take off your gloves before removing your isolation gown during doffing?

options.A: To make it easier to tie the gown strings behind your back for the next shift
options.B: To prevent contaminating your hands and clothing with germs on the outside of the gown
options.C: To ensure the gown remains sterile for the next healthcare worker
options.D: To save time while exiting the patient care area in a busy ward

explanation: You're doing great! Your gloves carry the most germs, so taking them off first stops you from accidentally spreading pathogens to your clean hands and uniform. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h4)

question: How does aseptic technique differ from everyday household cleaning?

options.A: Aseptic technique is only performed by medical doctors
options.B: Aseptic technique aims for the complete absence of disease-producing microbes
options.C: Household cleaning uses stronger bleach solutions than hospitals
options.D: Household cleaning is regulated by strict international health laws

explanation: While cleaning removes visible dirt, aseptic technique specifically targets invisible pathogens to protect patients during vulnerable procedures. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: A pregnant woman arrives at a clinic bleeding heavily, but the nurses cannot help because there is no blood or oxygen. Which delay is this?

options.A: First delay
options.B: Community delay
options.C: Third delay
options.D: Second delay

explanation: That's the third delay! It happens when the patient finally reaches the health facility, but the facility fails to provide adequate, quality care due to lack of supplies or staff. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h4)

question: In which part of the prostate gland does benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) usually start?

options.A: Transition zone
options.B: Seminal vesicle
options.C: Central zone
options.D: Peripheral zone

explanation: BPH mostly starts in the inner transition zone, which wraps tightly around the urethra. That's why it quickly causes trouble with passing urine. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h3)

question: You want to improve child health in a rural village. What is the best first step?

options.A: Distribute standard vitamins without checking local diets
options.B: Ask local mothers about their main health concerns
options.C: Build a modern pediatric ward immediately
options.D: Report village leaders to the ministry of health

explanation: Brilliant! Talking directly to the community helps you understand their real challenges instead of just guessing what they need. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why do surgeons sometimes place antibiotic-impregnated beads into a bone cavity after debridement?

options.A: To act as a permanent anchor for future muscle attachments
options.B: To deliver a high concentration of medication directly to the infection site
options.C: To attract white blood cells away from the rest of the body
options.D: To permanently replace missing calcium and strengthen the bone

explanation: Antibiotic beads release local medication directly into the wound bed at high levels without causing systemic toxicity. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h8)

question: What does the health-illness continuum primarily represent?

options.A: A sliding scale of a person's changing health state over time
options.B: A permanent record of a patient's genetic history
options.C: A strict diagnostic checklist for infectious diseases
options.D: A fixed medical category separating the healthy from the sick

explanation: The continuum demonstrates that health changes constantly rather than staying in a fixed state. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h1)

question: How can public health nurses use incidence data to check if an immunization campaign worked?

options.A: By calculating the average age of patients in the ward
options.B: By measuring the total money spent on medical supplies
options.C: By checking if the number of new infections drops over time
options.D: By counting the total number of hospital beds available

explanation: If a vaccination drive is successful, you should see the number of new infections (incidence) go way down. Awesome nursing logic! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: Why do we generally avoid giving live vaccines to pregnant women?

options.A: Live vaccines deactivate automatically in pregnant bloodstreams
options.B: Hormonal changes turn live viruses into strong bacteria
options.C: Pregnant women always develop permanent immunity instantly
options.D: There is a theoretical risk of harming the developing fetus

explanation: Live vaccines contain weakened germs that might pose risks during pregnancy, so we prefer using safe, inactivated options instead. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h3)

question: What makes keeping up a safety culture difficult in low-resource hospitals?

options.A: Severe staff shortages and frequent equipment limitations
options.B: An excess of highly trained specialist doctors
options.C: Complete absence of patient admissions
options.D: Too many safety policies written in complex languages

explanation: You got it! Heavy workloads, tired staff, and missing supplies make everyday safety practices tough to maintain. [learn more](GST319_U5_T3#GST319_U5_T3_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of priming extension tubing with normal saline before starting an IV?

options.A: To remove trapped air and prevent air embolisms
options.B: To warm the tubing up to body temperature
options.C: To test if the syringe plunger moves smoothly
options.D: To dilute any medication given later on

explanation: Clearing all air bubbles from the line stops air from entering the patient's bloodstream during cannulation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a core nursing responsibility for a patient on targeted receptor therapy?

options.A: Performing surgery to remove the endocrine glands
options.B: Providing emotional support for distressing physical side effects
options.C: Monitoring the patient closely for side effects related to hormone blockade
options.D: Educating the patient on the importance of taking medications regularly

explanation: Surgeons handle the operating room; nurses shine in assessment, patient education, emotional care, and managing side effects. You've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h7)

question: Why does the foetal body redirect blood to the brain and heart during low oxygen states?

options.A: To speed up the growth of skin and digestive tissues
options.B: To protect the most vital organs from permanent damage
options.C: To increase the overall temperature of the amniotic fluid
options.D: To prepare the lungs for breathing air after birth

explanation: The body prioritizes survival by ensuring oxygen-rich blood reaches critical centers like the brain and heart first. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h1)

question: What is a point source of water pollution?

options.A: A distinct, identifiable location like a factory pipe
options.B: Windblown dust falling randomly over a lake
options.C: Underground seepage from multiple small homes
options.D: Widespread rainfall runoff from a large farm

explanation: Point sources release pollutants from a single, fixed spot that is easy to spot and regulate. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse educator to know and use more than one teaching method?

options.A: Hospital management mandates a change of method every single week
options.B: Different learning objectives and situations require different instructional approaches
options.C: Using multiple methods is the only way to assign passing grades
options.D: Students lose their nursing license if they experience only one teaching style

explanation: Just like you wouldn't use the same nursing procedure for every patient, you can't teach anatomy theory the exact same way you teach emergency resuscitation skills. Variety helps concepts stick! [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of competency-based training over normal classroom lectures for PAC nurses?

options.A: It allows the training course to be completed in under one hour
options.B: It ensures learners prove practical clinical skill before treating patients
options.C: It focuses solely on reading policy documents and guidelines
options.D: It completely removes the need for any clinical supervisors

explanation: Competency-based learning is all about hands-on practice and actually mastering the skill, so you feel confident stepping into the clinical ward. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h4)

question: What is a common danger when researchers use very long or complex checklists during busy ward shifts?

options.A: Observer fatigue leading to rushed or guessed answers
options.B: Automatic rejection of the study by the ethics committee
options.C: Immediate breakdown of hospital computer networks
options.D: Patients refusing to take their prescribed medications

explanation: Keep it concise! When tools are too long and staff are tired, they lose focus and might just start guessing. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h6)

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is the primary nursing priority immediately after a patient returns from a cardiac catheterization via the femoral artery?

options.A: Removing the pressure dressing to inspect the exact puncture wound
options.B: Encouraging the patient to get out of bed and walk around the room
options.C: Checking the insertion site for bleeding and monitoring distal pulses
options.D: Administering a large dose of oral potassium supplements immediately

explanation: Arterial access carries a high risk of bleeding and loss of blood flow to the leg, so nurses must frequently check the puncture site and the pulse in the foot. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h2)

question: What term do qualitative researchers use instead of traditional statistical terms like validity and reliability?

options.A: Trustworthiness
options.B: Numeric accuracy
options.C: Precision testing
options.D: Generalizability

explanation: Well done! Because qualitative work deals with stories and feelings rather than numbers, we check its quality by looking at its 'trustworthiness'. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why must nurses work to eliminate personal bias regarding gender roles in the clinic?

options.A: Hospital management requires all nurses to pass a gender exam
options.B: Biases prevent nurses from dispensing medications properly
options.C: Ministry of health guidelines ban nurses from talking to men
options.D: Biased attitudes can make men feel unwelcome and drive them away from care

explanation: When nurses act judgmentally or ignore fathers, it reinforces the belief that health clinics are not meant for men. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: A patient who just had lung surgery is scared to cough because their incision hurts. What should you, the nurse, do first?

options.A: Tell the patient that coughing is optional and let them sleep all day.
options.B: Apply a tight chest binder to completely immobilize the chest wall.
options.C: Administer prescribed pain medication before encouraging controlled coughing exercises.
options.D: Report the patient immediately to the surgeon for emergency re-operation.

explanation: Wonderful clinical judgment! Controlling the pain first allows the patient to cough and clear their lungs safely without agony, preventing complications like collapsed lung areas. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of an Incident Command System (ICS) during a disaster?

options.A: To restrict healthcare workers from participating in field rescues
options.B: To automate financial audits for government ministries
options.C: To provide a standardized hierarchy for multi-agency collaboration
options.D: To prevent local community volunteers from assisting victims

explanation: The ICS sets a clear chain of command so different groups (like health workers, fire service, and police) can work together smoothly without stepping on each other's toes. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the recommended target range for endotracheal tube cuff pressure to prevent tracheal damage?

options.A: 60 to 70 cmH2O
options.B: 40 to 50 cmH2O
options.C: 20 to 30 cmH2O
options.D: 5 to 10 cmH2O

explanation: Maintaining cuff pressure between 20 and 30 cmH2O seals the airway adequately without cutting off blood flow to the tracheal lining. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is a major risk for patients taking immune checkpoint inhibitors (immunotherapy)?

options.A: The medication causes immediate permanent sterility in both male and female patients.
options.B: The boosted immune system may attack normal, healthy organs, causing widespread inflammation.
options.C: The drug destroys bone marrow production completely, requiring lifelong platelet transfusions.
options.D: The patient will instantly lose all hair follicles within forty-eight hours of the first dose.

explanation: You got it! Reviving the immune system is great for fighting cancer, but sometimes the revved-up immune cells accidentally attack healthy organs like the lungs or gut. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the cone-shaped tip attached to the otoscope head called?

options.A: A speculum
options.B: A stylus
options.C: A probe
options.D: A cannula

explanation: The speculum is the disposable or reusable cone attached to the otoscope that enters the ear canal. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h3)

question: A mother says she mixed her child's ORS packet into half a liter of water instead of a full liter. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to add extra sugar to balance out the high salt content
options.B: Instruct her to add another half-liter of water to the existing mixture and stir well
options.C: Allow her to feed the concentrated solution since it will work faster anyway
options.D: Discard the solution and help her mix a fresh batch correctly with one full liter of water

explanation: Guessing water amounts can throw off body chemistry. It is always safest to throw out the wrong mix and prepare a fresh, accurately measured batch. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h4)

question: What is the main job of Sertoli cells while sperm is being made?

options.A: Supporting and nourishing the developing sperm cells
options.B: Producing the alkaline fluid found in semen
options.C: Releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone into the blood
options.D: Carrying mature sperm through the vas deferens

explanation: You got it! Think of Sertoli cells as the 'nurse' cells of the testes—they look after the baby sperm cells and give them food and support while they grow. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient with yellow fever vomits dark, coffee-ground looking material. What is this classic clinical sign called?

options.A: Melena stool
options.B: Gastric sludge
options.C: Biliary reflux
options.D: Black vomit

explanation: Spot on! Bleeding inside the stomach mixing with digestive acids produces the famous 'black vomit' seen in severe cases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h4)

question: What is a major safety risk when dealing with pressurized gas cylinders as waste?

options.A: Gradual chemical corrosion of plastic containers
options.B: Spread of bacterial infections through the air
options.C: Risk of explosion when exposed to high heat
options.D: Attraction of radioactive dust particles

explanation: Pressurized containers can blow up violently if they get tossed into an incinerator or face extreme heat. Safety first! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the main reason to encourage plenty of fluids for a patient with metabolic joint disease?

options.A: To dilute the blood so that red blood cells multiply faster
options.B: To prevent the stomach from absorbing purines from digested food
options.C: To keep the skin moist and prevent breakdown around the joints
options.D: To help the kidneys flush out excess metabolic waste products and prevent crystal formation

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out uric acid before it has a chance to form painful crystals in the joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h8)

question: What type of statistics is mainly used in explanatory research to test hypotheses?

options.A: Decorative statistics
options.B: Inferential statistics
options.C: Fictional statistics
options.D: Historical statistics

explanation: You've got it! Inferential statistics help us test hypotheses and check if our findings are truly significant. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h7)

question: What big challenge do family members often face when they care round-the-clock for a relative with a severe physical disability?

options.A: Permanent immunity from chronic lifestyle diseases
options.B: Caregiver burnout and emotional exhaustion
options.C: Sudden loss of personal interest in healthcare
options.D: Automatic financial compensation from the state

explanation: Well done! Looking after someone 24/7 takes a heavy toll. Caregivers need care and support too so they don't burn out. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T11#GNS225_U5_T11_h3)

question: What is the main focus of 'staffing' in nursing management?

options.A: Creating policies for infection control
options.B: Designing the architectural layout of a new hospital building
options.C: Purchasing new lab equipment
options.D: Placing the right number of qualified nurses on the floor for every shift

explanation: Staffing is all about recruitment, scheduling, and making sure you have enough hands on deck. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why must a nurse researcher be extra careful when asking their own hospital patients to join a study?

options.A: Patients always know more about research than the nurses do
options.B: Patients might feel pressured to agree out of fear of poor care
options.C: Patients are legally barred from signing consent forms
options.D: Hospital management forbids nurses from talking to patients

explanation: Spot on! Patients might feel too scared to say 'no' because they worry it might affect the medical care they get from the ward. We must always make participation 100% voluntary! [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which position is commonly used to relieve pressure during an umbilical cord prolapse?

options.A: Flat supine position
options.B: Left lateral position only
options.C: Upright sitting position
options.D: Knee-chest position

explanation: Placing the mother in the knee-chest position uses gravity to keep the presenting fetal part off the compressed umbilical cord. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h8)

question: Why do registered nurses practice delegation during a heavy shift?

options.A: To manage heavy workloads and provide safe, efficient care
options.B: To shift legal blame for mistakes onto junior support staff
options.C: To comply with government orders regarding hospital staffing ratios
options.D: To avoid performing direct physical care for stable patients

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing work away because you're lazy—it's a smart teamwork tool to ensure every patient gets safe, timely care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is Vitamin K's main role when it comes to blood clotting?

options.A: It dissolves dangerous blood clots in the veins
options.B: It helps the liver produce important clotting proteins
options.C: It constricts damaged blood vessels instantly
options.D: It stimulates the bone marrow to make platelets

explanation: Vitamin K is like a helper vitamin that your liver needs to build essential clotting factors. Without it, your blood cannot clot properly! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T15#GNS215_U6_T15_h2)

question: A patient who eats a strict vegan diet and avoids all animal products is most at risk of lacking which nutrient?

options.A: Vitamin B12
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Vitamin B12 is mostly found in animal foods like meat, eggs, and dairy. Strict vegans often need to take a supplement to keep their B12 levels healthy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h3)

question: Why must you watch the baby closely with a CTG machine when giving an oxytocin drip?

options.A: Oxytocin makes the baby sleep deeply throughout the entire procedure.
options.B: Oxytocin causes the cervix to close up instead of opening further.
options.C: Oxytocin permanently lowers the mother's blood pressure to dangerous levels.
options.D: Oxytocin can cause uterine hyperstimulation, leading to reduced blood flow and fetal distress.

explanation: Spot on! Too much oxytocin can make contractions come too fast without resting breaks, cutting off oxygen to the baby. Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h7)

question: When is Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) most often used during fertility treatments?

options.A: When the female partner has irregular menstrual cycles
options.B: To prevent the transmission of common seasonal flus
options.C: Severe male factor infertility with very low sperm count
options.D: When the couple prefers natural conception at home

explanation: ICSI is a neat lab trick where embryologists inject a single, healthy sperm straight into an egg to bypass severe male fertility hurdles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h6)

question: When you take over a new shift, what do you accept regarding your assigned patients?

options.A: Financial responsibility for their hospital bills
options.B: Legal and professional accountability for their care
options.C: The obligation to discharge them by the end of the day
options.D: Full ownership of all past medical errors made by doctors

explanation: Taking over patients means you are now officially responsible for watching over them and giving them proper care during your shift. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h1)

question: What do we call the fraction of a drug that successfully reaches the bloodstream in an active, unchanged form?

options.A: Clearance rate
options.B: Half-life
options.C: Bioavailability
options.D: Volume of distribution

explanation: Bioavailability simply means 'how much active drug is actually available' to your body to do its job after the journey. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h6)

question: A patient is treated for scabies in your clinic. What must you tell them about the rest of people living in their house?

options.A: Family members should take oral antibiotics to prevent secondary boils
options.B: Household members only need treatment if they sleep in the same bed
options.C: Only family members who are scratching should visit the clinic for cream
options.D: All household contacts must be treated at the same time, regardless of symptoms

explanation: You've got it! Because scabies spreads before itching starts, treating everyone under the roof at the same time is the only way to kick it out for good. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h6)

question: Which popular fruit juice is well known for interfering with gut enzymes and dangerously raising blood levels of certain drugs?

options.A: Grapefruit juice
options.B: Filtered tap water
options.C: Fresh cow milk
options.D: Green tea infusion

explanation: Grapefruit juice is a classic pharmacological troublemaker! It blocks specific enzymes in your gut, letting way too much of a drug slip into your bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the most critical absolute contraindication for a standard barium swallow test?

options.A: Controlled type 2 diabetes
options.B: Suspected gastrointestinal perforation
options.C: A history of seasonal allergies
options.D: Mild chronic hypertension

explanation: If barium leaks outside a torn or perforated gut wall into the body cavities, it causes a severe, dangerous inflammatory reaction. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the main objective of the empowerment approach in health promotion?

options.A: Ensuring that government officials make all health decisions for citizens
options.B: Forcing communities to build modern hospitals using their own unpaid labor
options.C: Helping people gain the confidence and skills to take control of their own health
options.D: Relying solely on foreign pharmaceutical donations

explanation: Empowerment focuses on building self-reliance so communities can advocate for their own needs and solve local health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h6)

question: A nursing mum wants steady, long-lasting energy for her daily chores. What should you recommend she eat?

options.A: Pure cooking oils taken directly by the spoonful
options.B: Salt-free butter eaten in large morning portions
options.C: Simple refined sugars found in carbonated beverages
options.D: Complex carbohydrates like yams and whole grains

explanation: Complex carbs digest slowly and steadily. Foods like yams and whole grains give you the sustained energy needed to care for a newborn all day long! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h3)

question: What is a community health nurse's main job inside a flood relief camp?

options.A: Managing federal budgets for national security operations
options.B: Preventing disease outbreaks by promoting hygiene and managing basic health issues
options.C: Conducting police investigations into the cause of the flood
options.D: Constructing permanent concrete housing for all displaced families

explanation: You got it, nurse! In relief camps, keeping hygiene high and treating minor sicknesses stops outbreaks like cholera before they start. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h7)

question: In HIV testing, what do we mean by the term 'window period'?

options.A: The specific hours of the day when a testing clinic is open
options.B: The duration that antiretroviral drugs remain active in the body
options.C: The waiting time required to receive a laboratory confirmation
options.D: The time between exposure and when antibodies can be detected

explanation: Well done! The window period is the gap where someone has HIV, but tests can't pick up the antibodies yet, which can sometimes cause a false negative. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T10#GNS216_U6_T10_h3)

question: Which infection is most directly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Human papillomavirus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Human immunodeficiency virus

explanation: High-risk strains of human papillomavirus (HPV) can hang around in the cells of the cervix for years and eventually cause cell changes that lead to cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why might a woman with an epidural during labor not realize her bladder is getting too full?

options.A: Neural sensory blockade
options.B: Rapid increase in serum creatinine
options.C: Severe drop in blood glucose
options.D: Sudden loss of kidney function

explanation: An epidural numbs the lower body nerves, so the normal feeling of needing to pee is blocked. That's why midwives always check and help drain the bladder! Keep this in mind for your clinical postings. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h4)

question: Why would a doctor choose a nasal endoscope instead of a basic speculum exam?

options.A: To stop sudden nosebleeds in the front septum
options.B: To measure air pressure inside the cheek sinuses
options.C: To test the patient's sense of smell
options.D: To look deep inside the nasal passages and sinus openings

explanation: Nasal endoscopes use tiny cameras and lights to see past the front of the nose into deeper areas a regular speculum can't reach. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h4)

question: What percentage of total blood volume is typically made up of plasma?

options.A: 45 percent
options.B: 20 percent
options.C: 55 percent
options.D: 80 percent

explanation: Plasma makes up about 55 percent of your blood. It acts as the liquid highway carrying cells, nutrients, and waste products all around the body! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h2)

question: How should a nurse manager guide a brand-new student nurse doing a complex procedure for the very first time?

options.A: With complete independence and no supervision
options.B: With close supervision and clear, step-by-step guidance
options.C: By ignoring the procedure until the shift ends
options.D: By delegating the task entirely to another student

explanation: Beginners need high support and a watchful eye to keep patients safe and build their confidence. You'd want the same when learning a new skill! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the best immediate physical step to help reduce swelling right after a fresh injury?

options.A: Using a heating pad
options.B: Applying a cold pack
options.C: Placing a warm moist towel
options.D: Giving a deep tissue massage

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Cold constricts blood vessels, which slows down fluid pooling into the area and helps numb the sharp pain right away. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which type of surveillance involves public health workers actively visiting facilities to search for cases?

options.A: Sentinel surveillance
options.B: Active surveillance
options.C: Syndromic surveillance
options.D: Passive surveillance

explanation: Active surveillance means health staff take the initiative to go out and look for cases rather than waiting for reports to come in. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why do doctors start checking for fertility issues after just six months for women aged 35 and older?

options.A: To account for the faster decline in ovarian reserve and egg quality
options.B: Because older couples have more frequent sexual intercourse
options.C: To prevent the development of chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Because hormonal treatments work much faster in older women

explanation: Spot on! Egg quality and quantity change faster as women get older, so catching things early helps. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T19#GNS312_U1_T19_h1)

question: Where do most nutrient pollutants like nitrogen and phosphorus in water bodies come from?

options.A: Thermal discharge from power plants
options.B: Dissolved heavy metal mining
options.C: Agricultural fertilizer runoff
options.D: Floating physical plastic waste

explanation: Spot on! Fertilizers wash off farmlands during rains and flow into nearby streams and lakes, causing massive weed and algae growth. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the golden rule right after using a disposable injection needle?

options.A: Place the used syringe inside a paper envelope for disposal
options.B: Drop it straight into a puncture-resistant sharps container
options.C: Break the needle tip off to prevent accidental skin pricks
options.D: Recap the needle carefully using a one-handed scoop method

explanation: Never recap or bend used needles! Drop them instantly into a rigid sharps container to keep yourself and others safe from accidental pricks. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a common misconception about publishing a research paper?

options.A: It requires writing down the methods and study results
options.B: It takes time and careful adherence to journal guidelines
options.C: It helps hospital administrators make policy decisions
options.D: It automatically changes clinical behavior at the bedside

explanation: That's a tricky one, but you've got it! Just publishing a paper doesn't automatically change clinical practice; nurses still need active encouragement and training to apply it. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which past surgery is most likely to cause scar tissue (adhesions) that could affect future fertility?

options.A: Pelvic surgery or surgery inside the lower belly
options.B: Appendectomy on the arm
options.C: Tonsillectomy
options.D: Knee arthroscopy

explanation: Surgeries close to the reproductive organs can leave behind small bands of scar tissue that might twist or block the fallopian tubes. Good to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a key safety duty for a nurse when giving a patient a new walking aid?

options.A: Disassembling the device daily for thorough cleaning
options.B: Painting the device to match the patient's favorite color
options.C: Restricting the patient from using it outside the hospital
options.D: Ensuring proper fit and teaching safe usage techniques

explanation: Safety first! If a walking aid doesn't fit right or isn't used properly, it can easily lead to accidental falls or injuries. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h5)

question: What is a common social penalty for a woman spotted visiting a family planning clinic in a stigmatized community?

options.A: Being labeled as promiscuous by neighbors
options.B: Receiving a free scholarship for her children
options.C: Being appointed as the village head
options.D: Winning a local agricultural prize

explanation: Correct! Community stigma unfortunately leads people to make false assumptions about the moral character of women seeking birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h7)

question: Why is it important to assess the patient's perception before delivering bad news?

options.A: To determine if the patient has insurance coverage
options.B: To make sure the doctor does not have to speak at all
options.C: To align your explanation with what they already understand and expect
options.D: To test if the patient read their medical chart correctly

explanation: Checking perception helps you tailor the message so you do not overwhelm them with information that contradicts or far exceeds their current understanding. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h4)

question: A diabetic patient needs a clear fluid diet after surgery. What should you look out for?

options.A: Provide regular sweetened fruit juices to boost immediate energy.
options.B: Withhold all fluids until insulin can be completely stopped.
options.C: Ensure the patient receives sugar-free clear liquid options.
options.D: Allow the patient to eat any sweet full fluid item desired.

explanation: Even on liquid diets, blood sugar control matters. Always reach for sugar-free options to keep their glucose stable. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h5)

question: Which special cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: Parietal cells
options.C: Goblet cells
options.D: Mucus neck cells

explanation: Parietal cells are the acid-makers of the stomach, and they also produce intrinsic factor which helps your body absorb vitamin B12. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T3#GNS121_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is often the primary cure for a hormone-secreting endocrine tumor?

options.A: Complete removal of the liver and spleen
options.B: Lifelong high-dose antibiotic therapy
options.C: Drinking large amounts of plain water
options.D: Surgical removal of the tumor
